newsitem.title: USA: Schmalbach sees no layoffs from U.S. buy.
newsitem.headline: Schmalbach sees no layoffs from U.S. buy.

text.p: German packaging company Schmalbach-Lubeca AG foresees no layoffs from its purchase of a Johnson Controls Inc plastics unit in the United States, Schmalbach's chairman and chief executive said Thursday.

The executive, Hanno Fiedler, told Reuters the approximately $650 million acquisition of Johnson Controls' PET plastics division should be completed by the end of the month pending approval by European anti-trust regulators.
"We don't see any victims as far as head counts are concerned," he said, adding there was little overlap between the unit and Schmalbach's current operations.
"For the people in the United States, essentially nothing will change, except the name over the gate."

Schmalbach, a unit of German utility VIAG AG, announced the prospective purchase in early December. The Johnson Controls unit has about 2,700 employees, with 1,400 in the United States and a total of 29 plants in the United States, Europe and South America.

The plastics unit, headquartered in Manchester, Mich., has annual sales of about $800 million and is the second biggest producer of PET plastic in the United States. PET is an acronym for the polymer polyethylene terephthalate and is used in packaging, especially for beverages.

Fiedler, who was in the United States to meet investors, said the purchase would ready Schmalbach to expand into a worldwide market. Schmalbach is the largest producer of PET plastic in Europe and the acquisition will give it about 15 percent of the world market.
The Johnson Controls' unit also has technological expertise in such areas as hot-filling and recycling. The purchase will give Schmalbach's added clout with resin suppliers, Fiedler said.
Schmalbach's other divisions make such products as beverage cans and closures. Fiedler expected total sales of about four billion marks, or $2.6 billion, in 1996, about the same as the year before.
The company had earnings of a "big black zero" in 1995 and expects them to rise to 50 million marks, or about $33 million, this year, Fiedler said.
Fiedler, then an executive at TRW Inc, became Schmalbach-Lubeca's chief executive and chairman in January 1996 as part of a management shakeup.
Asked if he felt pressure from VIAG, the parent company, to improve performance, he said: "As far as 1996 is concerned, what we promised we delivered."
Although Fiedler would not disclose the terms of the purchase, he said reports the acquisition would cost a billion marks, or about $650 million, were "not far off."
